observed_result.criterion: (a) From the worker-only environment the CA is absent and signing through the worker socket fails. (b) The child certificate (principal subset, earlier valid_before) is refused on ca2 and, after its own expiry, on ca1 while the parent still works. (c) No CA private material in the worker/child path. Fail: CA reachable from the worker path; child broader or longer than its parent.
observed_result.summary: Observed: the fixture CA was held by an issuer agent (0700 dir containing just its socket) that signed the parent {p-host1,p-host2} and child {p-host1} certificates (rc 0). Read back from the issued certificates: child principals a strict subset, child valid_before 840 s earlier than the parent's. From the worker-only environment: ssh-add -L showed 2 entries (K_env, certificate) and no CA; ssh-keygen -U -s <CA pub> through the worker socket rc 255, no certificate written. Servers: child on ca1 rc 0 before its expiry; child on ca2 rc 255 ('Certificate does not contain an authorized principal'); after child expiry, child on ca1 rc 255 ('Certificate invalid: expired') while the parent still logged in on ca1 and ca2 (rc 0). Scan of worker/child files (4), agent argv/env and worker env: 0 hits of CA material. Verdict pass against the stated (endpoint) criterion. Findings, not part of the criterion: (1) a same-user process given the issuer socket path obtained a certificate (rc 0); (2) the fixture CA private key FILE stayed readable by the same user from the worker-only environment (mode -rw-------, owned by the harness uid) for the whole experiment. So the 'worker path' separation is an environment and agent-endpoint boundary only, not an OS or file-access boundary.

limitations: OpenSSH mechanism evidence only: host client /usr/bin/ssh (OpenSSH_10.3p1, LibreSSL 3.3.6, macOS) against sshd (OpenSSH_10.0p2 Debian-7+deb13u4, OpenSSL 3.5.6 7 Apr 2026) in disposable Docker fixture containers. No Heimdall code exists or ran; this is not evidence of Heimdall behavior.

Not desktop-lock, sleep, logout, reboot or secure-store evidence: the dedicated agents are plain ssh-agent processes in an unlocked session started by the harness. Lock continuity remains open (owner-run probes).
Single machine: macOS 27.0 arm64 with Docker Desktop (linux VM). No native Windows/WSL or Linux-host evidence. The openssh-server package version is observed, not pinned (apt floats at image build).
Fixture sshd sets PerSourcePenalties no, unlike the OpenSSH 10 default.
Requirement IDs are listed for traceability; this record is not by itself evidence that any product requirement is met (tests/evidence/README.md).

Independent review M00-review-g04 (tests/evidence/artifacts/m00-wf2/review-g04.json) re-ran the earlier version of these experiments from scratch and refuted the earlier '-O stop: admissions stopped' conclusion; this record comes from the corrected harness (task M00-T04-G04-fix). The corrections themselves have not been independently re-reviewed.

Issuer, worker and child are the same OS user. Separation is by agent endpoint only; a same-user process that knows the issuer socket path can obtain signatures (recorded as the E5-same-user-boundary finding). Stronger isolation needs a separate OS account/service or external issuer (spec 7.3).

The attenuation (child principals a subset, earlier valid_before) was chosen by the harness when it asked the issuer agent to sign; ssh-agent itself enforces no issuance policy. What was observed is that the issued certificates carry the narrower values and that the servers enforce them.
Scan for CA material covered the worker/child temp dirs, the worker/child agent processes' argv and environment (counts only, never printed) and the worker command environment, not process memory.

The fixture CA private key FILE (tests/fixtures/ssh/runtime/keys/user_ca, loaded into the issuer agent) stayed on disk and readable by the same OS user from the worker-only environment for the whole experiment (finding E5-ca-file-readable-by-same-user). 'No CA material in the worker path' therefore means: not in the worker/child files, agent argv/env or worker env, and not reachable through the worker agent endpoint. It is an environment and endpoint boundary only, not a file-access boundary.
